test_title: SSC MTS 2023 Official Paper (Held On: 12 Sept, 2023 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: A seller marked the price of a sofa 25% more than its cost price. If he allows 12% discount on the marked price to the customer, then what is his gain percentage? If the cost price of the sofa is Rs. 15,000, then what is his gain money?
solution:
**Given:**

Cost price (CP) of the sofa = Rs. 15,000

Marked price (MP) is 25% more than CP

Discount allowed = 12%

**Formula Used:**

Marked Price (MP) = CP + 25% of CP

Discounted Price (Selling Price, SP) = MP - 12% of MP

Gain Percentage = [(SP - CP) / CP] × 100

Gain Money = SP - CP

**Calculation:**

We have,

⇒ CP = Rs. 15,000

⇒ MP = CP + 25% of CP

⇒ MP = 15,000 + (25/100) × 15,000

⇒ MP = 15,000 + 3,750

⇒ MP = Rs. 18,750

⇒ SP = MP - 12% of MP

⇒ SP = 18,750 - (12/100) × 18,750

⇒ SP = 18,750 - 2,250

⇒ SP = Rs. 16,500

⇒ Gain Percentage = [(SP - CP) / CP] × 100

⇒ Gain Percentage = [(16,500 - 15,000) / 15,000] × 100

⇒ Gain Percentage = [1,500 / 15,000] × 100

⇒ Gain Percentage = 0.10 × 100

⇒ **Gain Percentage = 10%**

⇒ Gain Money = SP - CP

⇒ Gain Money = 16,500 - 15,000

⇒ Gain Money = Rs. 1,500

**∴ The correct answer is option 3: 10%; Rs. 1,500**
